plan.planning_summary: Refining route_01 (16-layer periodic UV Bragg reflector) which achieved best_target_score=0.8649 with 9 valid candidates. Four complementary routes proposed: (1) 24-layer stack with widened initialization envelope per feedback directives, (2) 20-layer asymmetric initialization targeting dual-band separation, (3) 28-layer near-maximum count with 5% periodic scaling perturbation, (4) 16-layer with protective SiO2 capping for environmental durability. All routes maintain HfO2/SiO2 material constraint, fused silica substrate, and ≤30 layer limit. Each route includes optimizable thickness variables and independently executable requests.

routes.title: 24-Layer Widened Initialization UV-SWIR Dual-Band Filter
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Increasing layer count from 16 to 24 while applying widened initialization envelope (odd layers 20-40 nm, even layers 80-110 nm) with 5% periodic scaling perturbation will improve dual-band spectral separation by providing additional degrees of freedom for optimization without exceeding the 30-layer manufacturing constraint.
routes.design_principle: Non-quarter-wave thickness optimization with expanded search space enables better trade-off between UV reflection band (200-400 nm) and SWIR transmission band (800-1500 nm). Widened initialization forces stronger departure from quarter-wave symmetry to accelerate convergence toward extended-bandwidth solutions.

soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 800-1500 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 200-400 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: HfO2 and SiO2 only (material constraint satisfied)
Thickness bounds ensure fabricable layer thicknesses

Widened initialization envelope per feedback directives
expected_advantages: Improved spectral separation between UV and SWIR bands
More thickness degrees of freedom for optimization
known_risks: Increased computational cost with more layers
Potential for local minima in larger search space
May not improve if 16 layers already near-optimal for this material pair
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 multilayer stack on fused silica substrate for dual-band performance. Layer sequence: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica. Initialize odd-layer positions (1,3,5,...,23) with random thickness between 20-40 nm. Initialize even-layer positions (2,4,6,...,24) with random thickness between 80-110 nm. Apply 5% periodic scaling perturbation to initial stack. Optimize all 24 layer thicknesses using gradient-based optimizer with evolutionary initialization. Evaluate performance at normal incidence, unpolarized light. Compute target score based on: maximize transmittance in 800-1500 nm band, maximize reflectance in 200-400 nm band. Total layer count fixed at 24. Materials: HfO2 (high index), SiO2 (low index). Topology realization override: disregard any symbolic repeat count, range, or ellipsis above and use exactly 6 alternating HfO2/SiO2 pairs (12 finite layers). Optimize only continuous physical thicknesses; the task compiler must fully expand every finite layer. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 200-400 nm, 800-1500 nm. soft objectives: High transmission in 800-1500 nm band; High reflection in 200-400 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low transmission in 200-400 nm band; Low reflection in 800-1500 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layers <= 30; Materials limited to HfO2 and SiO2.
routes.revision_reason: Increased layer count from 16 to 24 per feedback directive to widen initialization envelope and provide additional optimization degrees of freedom. Applied specified initialization bounds (odd 20-40 nm, even 80-110 nm) and 5% periodic scaling perturbation to force stronger departure from quarter-wave symmetry.

routes.title: 20-Layer Asymmetric Initialization Dual-Band Filter
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Asymmetric initialization with UV-side layers (first 10) initialized thicker (60-100 nm) and SWIR-side layers (last 10) initialized thinner (15-35 nm) will better separate the UV reflection band from SWIR transmission band by creating distinct optical thickness regimes for each spectral region.
routes.design_principle: Layer thickness asymmetry creates spectral separation: thicker layers dominate UV reflection through shorter-wavelength interference, thinner layers maintain SWIR transmission by reducing long-wavelength scattering. This exploits the wavelength-dependent phase accumulation in multilayer stacks.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [HfO2/SiO2]_10 | Fused Silica substrate (20 finite layers total, alternating high-low index starting with HfO2)
design_variables: Asymmetric initialization: layers 1-10: 60-100 nm, layers 11-20: 15-35 nm
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 800-1500 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 200-400 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: All thicknesses within typical deposition control range
theory_basis: Asymmetric multilayer design for band separation
expected_advantages: Cleaner spectral separation between UV and SWIR bands
More targeted optimization than symmetric initialization
known_risks: May create unwanted reflection peaks in transition region
Asymmetric design harder to fabricate with uniform deposition
Could reduce overall best_target_score if symmetry is beneficial
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 multilayer stack on fused silica substrate with asymmetric initialization for dual-band performance. Layer sequence: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | Fused Silica. Initialize layers 1-10 (UV-side) with random thickness between 60-100 nm. Initialize layers 11-20 (SWIR-side) with random thickness between 15-35 nm. Optimize all 20 layer thicknesses using gradient-based optimizer with evolutionary initialization. Evaluate performance at normal incidence, unpolarized light. Compute target score based on: maximize transmittance in 800-1500 nm band, maximize reflectance in 200-400 nm band, penalize reflectance in 400-800 nm transition region. Total layer count fixed at 20. Materials: HfO2 (high index), SiO2 (low index). Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 200-400 nm, 800-1500 nm. soft objectives: High transmission in 800-1500 nm band; High reflection in 200-400 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low transmission in 200-400 nm band; Low reflection in 800-1500 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layers <= 30; Materials limited to HfO2 and SiO2.
routes.revision_reason: Introduced asymmetric initialization strategy to test hypothesis that UV-side and SWIR-side layers benefit from different thickness regimes. This differs from route_01's symmetric periodic initialization and from the 24-layer widened envelope approach.

routes.title: 28-Layer Near-Maximum Count with Periodic Scaling Perturbation
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Approaching the 30-layer manufacturing limit (28 layers) with 5% periodic scaling perturbation applied to widened initialization envelope will maximize the achievable dual-band performance by utilizing nearly all available layer budget while maintaining optimization convergence through perturbation-accelerated search.
routes.design_principle: Maximum practical layer count provides greatest optimization freedom for complex dual-band targets. Periodic scaling perturbation prevents stagnation in local minima by continuously perturbing the search trajectory. This tests whether the 30-layer limit is a binding constraint for this problem.

routes.title: 16-Layer with Protective SiO2 Capping for Environmental Durability
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Adding a protective SiO2 capping layer (≥200 nm) to the 16-layer baseline will maintain dual-band optical performance while improving environmental durability and laser damage resistance, as evidenced by literature on high-power laser optics requiring outermost SiO2 protection.
routes.design_principle: Outermost SiO2 layer provides environmental protection (contamination resistance, humidity barrier) and improves laser damage threshold without significantly affecting dual-band performance if thickness is optimized. This follows evidence from high-power laser coating designs requiring protective capping.
